subject: Chemistry
title: Atomic Structure
summary: Atoms contain electrons (Thomson), a tiny dense positive nucleus (Rutherford) with protons and neutrons (Chadwick). Rutherford's model could not explain atomic stability or line spectra.
Light behaves as waves and as photons of energy E = hν. The photoelectric effect and the line spectrum of hydrogen proved that energy is quantised.
Bohr's model of hydrogen-like atoms quantises angular momentum (mvr = nh/2π) and gives energies Eₙ = −13.6 Z²/n² eV, explaining the hydrogen spectrum.
Quantum mechanics replaced orbits with orbitals. Four quantum numbers (n, l, m_l, m_s) describe each electron; orbitals fill by the Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle and Hund's rule.

formulas.name: Photoelectric effect
formulas.formula: hν = φ + K_max;  K_max = eV₀;  φ = hν₀
formulas.mistake: Intensity changes the number of electrons, not their maximum energy.

formulas.name: Radius of Bohr orbit
formulas.when: Size of orbits in H-like species (H, He⁺, Li²⁺).
formulas.note: r grows as n² but shrinks as 1/Z.

formulas.name: Rydberg formula
formulas.note: Lyman n₁ = 1 (UV), Balmer n₁ = 2 (visible), Paschen 3, Brackett 4, Pfund 5 (IR).

formulas.name: Number of spectral lines
formulas.formula: from level n down to 1: n(n − 1)/2
formulas.when: Lines emitted by a sample of excited atoms.

formulas.name: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle
formulas.when: Limits on knowing position and momentum together.
formulas.mistake: It is a fundamental limit, not a measuring-instrument problem.

formulas.name: Quantum numbers
formulas.when: Describing an orbital and an electron.

formulas.name: Nodes
formulas.formula: radial nodes = n − l − 1;  angular nodes = l;  total = n − 1

formulas.name: Orbital capacity
formulas.when: Maximum electrons in s, p, d, f and in a shell.

formulas.name: (n + l) rule
formulas.formula: lower (n + l) fills first; if equal, lower n fills first

topics.title: Discovery of subatomic particles
topics.explain: Electron: cathode rays, e/m measured by J.J. Thomson; charge by Millikan's oil-drop experiment. Proton: canal (anode) rays. Neutron: Chadwick (1932). Atomic number Z = protons; mass number A = protons + neutrons. Isotopes: same Z (¹H, ²H); isobars: same A (⁴⁰Ar, ⁴⁰Ca).

topics.title: Atomic models
topics.explain: Thomson: plum pudding. Rutherford (α-scattering on gold foil): most of the atom is empty, with a tiny dense positive nucleus; failed because an orbiting electron should radiate and spiral in. Bohr fixed this for hydrogen-like atoms only.

topics.title: Electromagnetic radiation
topics.explain: c = νλ. Black-body radiation and the photoelectric effect needed Planck's quantum idea: energy comes in packets hν. Line (atomic) spectra are like fingerprints of elements.

topics.title: Limitations of Bohr's model
topics.explain: Works only for one-electron species, cannot explain fine structure, the Zeeman (magnetic) and Stark (electric) effects, or chemical bonding, and contradicts the uncertainty principle by giving exact orbits.

topics.title: Quantum mechanical model
topics.explain: Schrödinger's equation gives wave functions ψ; |ψ|² is the probability density. An orbital is the region where finding the electron is most probable. Shapes: s orbitals are spherical, p dumb-bell shaped (px, py, pz), d mostly clover-leaf (dz² is special).

topics.title: Filling rules
topics.explain: Aufbau: lowest energy first. Pauli: no two electrons have the same four quantum numbers. Hund: in degenerate orbitals, electrons occupy singly with parallel spins before pairing. Half-filled and fully filled subshells are extra stable: Cr = [Ar]3d⁵4s¹, Cu = [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹.

topics.title: Energy of orbitals
topics.explain: In hydrogen, energy depends only on n (2s = 2p). In many-electron atoms it depends on n and l, because inner electrons shield outer ones differently (s penetrates most).
